tour.name: Rainbow Mountain Private Trek from Cusco: Vinicunca & the Red Valley
tour.subtitle: A private high-Andean day with a licensed mountain guide and car: breakfast in the village of Cusipata, the walk past alpaca herds to the striped summit of Vinicunca at 5,036 metres, the Red Valley viewpoint and the glacier of Ausangate, with oxygen and a first-aid kit carried.

tour.overview:
Southeast of Cusco, in the Vilcanota range near the sacred glacier of Ausangate, a mountain striped with bands of colour emerged from under the melting ice and snow in the last decades. Vinicunca, the Rainbow Mountain, owes its red, yellow, green and purple stripes to layers of sediment rich in iron, sulphur and other minerals. It has become one of the most popular hikes in Peru.

This private trek takes you there with a licensed mountain guide and a car, at your own pace. After breakfast in a village, you walk up from the trailhead past alpaca herds to the summit, look out over the striped ridges and the Red Valley with Ausangate behind, and return for lunch.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 13 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cusco
• Type: private trek with licensed mountain guide, private car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: hard; about 4 hours walking at 4,600 to 5,036 metres

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Vilcanota valley at dawn.
• Vinicunca, the Rainbow Mountain.
• The Red Valley.
• Ausangate glacier.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private guide sets the pace for your group, carries oxygen and adapts the route; we start early to reach the summit before the crowds and the afternoon clouds.

WHO IT SUITS
Fit, acclimatised walkers and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are new to altitude or prefer easier walks, choose our Moray and Maras tour or the Sacred Valley.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Only attempt this hike after at least two or three days in Cusco. Horses can be hired from local families for part of the way up. The weather changes fast: it can snow even in the dry season.

days.name: Breakfast in Cusipata, the trek to Vinicunca, the Red Valley and lunch
days.description:
What to expect: the Rainbow Mountain at your own pace, with a private mountain guide, car, fees, meals and oxygen.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 4:00 and drive south-east along the Vilcanota valley, about two and a half hours, with a stop for breakfast in the village of Cusipata. The road then climbs a side valley to the trailhead at about 4,600 metres.

You walk up a wide trail through a high valley, past stone corrals and herds of alpacas and llamas tended by Quechua families, with the white dome of Ausangate, 6,384 metres high, ahead. The last stretch to the ridge is steep; your guide keeps the pace slow and checks how everyone feels, and horses led by local families can carry you most of the way if needed. From the viewpoint at 5,036 metres, the mountain's stripes spread before you, and on the other side the Red Valley rolls away in waves of rust-red hills. If conditions allow, you walk a short loop to look down into the Red Valley.

You walk back down to the trailhead and drive to Cusipata or Pitumarca for a hearty lunch, then return to Cusco, arriving at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
04:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
06:30 – Breakfast in Cusipata.
08:00 – Start of the trek.
10:00 – Summit of Vinicunca.
10:45 – Red Valley viewpoint.
12:30 – Back at the trailhead.
13:30 – Lunch.
17:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Palccoyo, an easier alternative 'rainbow mountain' with three striped ridges, can replace Vinicunca.
• Your guide carries oxygen and turns back if anyone shows signs of altitude sickness.
• Bring cash for a horse if you might want one.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed mountain guide, entrance fees, breakfast and lunch, oxygen and first aid, water and snacks, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: horse hire, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How hard is it?
faq.answer: It is short, about 4 hours in total, but at very high altitude. Most fit, acclimatised walkers manage it at a slow pace.

faq.question: How long should we acclimatise first?
faq.answer: At least two or three days in Cusco or the Sacred Valley before attempting the hike.

faq.question: Can we ride a horse?
faq.answer: Yes. Local families rent horses for most of the climb; the last steep section is on foot. Payment is in cash on the spot.

faq.question: Is there an easier option?
faq.answer: Yes. Palccoyo has similar colours with a much easier walk of about 1 hour at slightly lower altitude.

faq.question: Are meals included?
faq.answer: Yes, breakfast and lunch, plus snacks and water.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Only for older, fit and acclimatised children. We suggest Palccoyo for families.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: No. The trail is steep and at extreme altitude.

faq.question: What happens if someone feels unwell?
faq.answer: Your guide carries oxygen and a first-aid kit and will descend with you; the car is never far from the trailhead.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Warm layers, a windproof and waterproof jacket, gloves, a hat, sunglasses, sun cream and hiking shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to September for the clearest skies. In the rainy season, snow can cover the stripes.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
